notes: The Arduino Nano Matter and Grove 8x8 RGB LED Matrix are not in the catalogue, so I added them as new part types. Their port lists are simplified to the pins this project uses, plus a few power and reset pins.
The diagram image was not available. The wiring follows the text: the matrix gets 3.3V and GND from the Nano Matter and talks to it over I2C (SDA and SCL).
The photo shows the board plugged into the breadboard and the matrix attached by a Grove cable. I modelled the Grove cable as four jumper wires, each running from a breadboard hole to a matrix pin.
The breadboard hole positions are assumed, not taken from the tutorial. I used 5t.a and 6t.a for 3V3 and GND, and 5b.f and 6b.f for SDA and SCL.
The Nano Matter's SDA and SCL pin positions on the real header are assumed. The tutorial only says the matrix uses I2C.
The USB-C cable plugs into the Nano Matter's USB port, which is not modelled as a named port.
Not included as parts: the Eero Thread border router, the Alexa speaker, and the phone app. They are network or software items, not part of the circuit.
